# Staff Augmentation vs Consulting: Costs Compared | MV.tech Solutions

URL: https://mvtech.solutions/insights/staff-augmentation-vs-project-consulting-vs-recruitment/
Description: Staff augmentation vs consulting: who directs the work, what each costs for the same eight-week project, and when a permanent hire is the better choice.
Last modified: 2026-11-26

Engagement models

## Staff augmentation vs project-based consulting: cost, control and when to hire instead

Staff augmentation vs consulting: who directs the work, what each costs for the same eight-week project, and when a permanent hire is the better choice.

By Meet Vaghasia, Founder & Lead Engineer · Published September 10, 2026 · Updated November 26, 2026 · 7 min read

In brief

- Choose ascoped projectwhen the outcome is clear and you want someone else accountable for delivering it.
- Choosestaff augmentationwhen the work is ongoing or still taking shape and you want senior capacity working under your own direction.
- Choosepermanent recruitmentwhen the role will exist for years and belongs inside your organization.
- Compare both proposals against the same deliverable, including the time your own team will spend. See theeight-week cost example.
Perhaps you have a warehouse migration to finish and a data platform to run afterward. One of those jobs has a finish line. The other needs someone to own it each month. That difference changes what you should ask a supplier to price.

### The three models, defined

#### Scoped project consulting

You describe an outcome; the consultancy proposes a scope with deliverables, milestones and acceptance criteria, then delivers it. The consultancy directs its own people and is accountable for the result. Typical examples: a first data pipeline and reporting layer, an internal application, an automation of a specific process, a knowledge assistant over a defined document set.

#### Staff augmentation (embedded consultants or a dedicated team)

Senior specialists join your team for an agreed capacity and duration, working in your tools, your rituals and your hours, under the direction of your technical leads. You own the backlog and the priorities; the consultancy supplies the people, the continuity and the quality bar. Typical examples: a data engineer alongside your product team for two quarters, an AI engineer to build out an assistant your team has designed, additional senior developers during a delivery crunch.

#### Technology recruitment

You hire a permanent employee into your organization. A recruitment partner helps define the role, find and assess candidates and coordinate the process; you make the hiring decision and employ the person directly. Typical examples: a head of data, a lead engineer for a new product, a permanent platform team.

### Side by side

Engagement models compared
| Question | Scoped project | Staff augmentation | Permanent recruitment |
| Who directs the day-to-day work? | The consultancy, against an agreed scope | Your technical leads | You, as the employer |
| Who carries delivery risk? | Shared, with the consultancy accountable for the scope | Mostly you; the consultancy is accountable for the person's quality and continuity | You |
| How quickly does it start? | After scoping, typically one to three weeks | Usually fastest once a fit is confirmed | Slowest: weeks to months depending on the role |
| Best when | The outcome is clear and bounded | The work is ongoing or still emerging | The role is long-term and core to the business |
| Cost structure | Fixed or milestone-based price for the scope | Agreed capacity and duration, priced accordingly | A recruitment fee plus ongoing salary and overheads |
| Knowledge stays with | You, via documentation and handover | Your team, because the work happens inside it | You, as long as the employee stays |
| Flexibility to stop or change | At milestone boundaries | High, within the notice terms | Low; hiring is a long-term commitment |

### Is staff augmentation cheaper than project-based consulting?

It depends on the hours the work will take and who will manage it. For staff augmentation, multiply the agreed rate by the capacity you expect to use. For a scoped project, add the milestone fees. In both cases, include your own team’s time for access, decisions, testing and handover.

#### Two ways to price the same eight-week migration

Say you need one pipeline moved and one finance report checked against the original. The example below uses fictional US dollar amounts. Substitute the figures from your proposals, including what an hour of your technical lead’s time costs your business.

Illustrative cost of delivering the same pipeline and signed-off report
| Budget item | Embedded engineer | Scoped project |
| Supplier cost | $16,000 for 20 hours a week over eight weeks | $17,000 for the agreed milestone |
| Your technical lead’s time | 20 hours at $100 = $2,000 | 5 hours at $100 = $500 |
| Estimated total | $18,000 | $17,500 |
The project quote starts $1,000 higher and costs $500 less once you include internal time. That comparison assumes the engineer can finish within 160 hours and that both proposals include reconciliation and handover. Ask what an extra source system or two weeks of post-launch fixes would cost before deciding.

### IT, AI and cloud consulting vs staff augmentation

The comparison works the same way whatever the specialism. In consulting, the supplier is accountable for an agreed outcome. In staff augmentation, you direct the people and own the outcome yourself.

- IT consulting vs staff augmentation.Consulting delivers an assessed system, a plan or a finished piece of work against a scope. Staff augmentation adds engineers or administrators to a team you already manage.
- AI consulting vs staff augmentation.Choose consulting when you still need to decide which use case is worth building and how it will be evaluated. Choose augmentation when your team has designed the system and needs an AI engineer to build it under your direction.
- Cloud consulting vs staff augmentation.Choose consulting for an architecture decision, a migration plan or a cost review. Choose augmentation for ongoing platform work that your leads will prioritize week by week.
The two can follow each other. A short consulting engagement settles the scope and architecture, and one of the same engineers then stays on as augmented capacity for the build.

### How to decide

#### Start from the shape of the work

If you can write the outcome on one page with acceptance criteria, it is a project. If you can only describe a stream of work and a direction, it is capacity, which points to augmentation. If you can describe a role that will still exist in three years, it is a hire.

#### Then consider who should be in control

Project consulting suits teams that want to buy an outcome and get on with their own work. Augmentation suits teams with strong technical leadership who want more senior hands without giving up direction. Recruitment suits organizations building durable in-house capability.

#### Then think about risk and reversibility

A project has a natural end and clear acceptance, which limits the downside. Augmentation is easy to scale up or down. A permanent hire is the largest commitment and the hardest to reverse, which is why it deserves the most careful brief.

### Common mistakes

- Buying a project when you need a team.Fixed scopes fight with emerging requirements. If the roadmap is uncertain, embed people instead.
- Buying "staff augmentation" that is really outsourcing.If you never meet the engineers and cannot direct them, it is not augmentation, whatever the contract says.
- Hiring permanently for a temporary spike.Six months of intense delivery followed by maintenance is a job for consultants, not a new headcount line.
- Treating recruitment and consulting as interchangeable.They have different scopes, fees and obligations. A good partner will tell you which one you are actually asking for.

### Combining the models

When a backlog extends past the first migration, you might bring in a data engineer to work alongside your lead. If several pipelines, models and reports have to move together, an offshore data engineering team can cover that mix. When someone will own the platform year-round, compare those costs with a permanent employee’s salary, benefits and the one-time cost of recruiting the right person.

To get a comparison for your own team, share the first deliverable, who can manage the work and roughly how much time you need covered. Write a hiring brief.

### Frequently asked questions

**What is the difference between staff augmentation and consulting?**
In staff augmentation, specialists join your team and your leads direct their work; you pay for agreed capacity and duration. In consulting, the supplier is accountable for an agreed outcome and directs its own people; you pay by scope or milestone. Choose augmentation for ongoing or changing work and consulting for a result with a clear finish.

**Which costs less, staff augmentation or project consulting?**
Compare the cost of the hours you would buy with the milestone fee for the same deliverable. Add the time your staff will spend managing and checking the work. The lower supplier fee can cost more overall if it requires substantially more internal time.

**Is staff augmentation the same as outsourcing?**
No. In staff augmentation, named consultants work inside your team under your direction, in your tools and your hours. In outsourcing, a vendor takes over a function or a scope and directs its own people. Augmentation keeps control and knowledge with you; outsourcing trades some of that for a managed outcome.

**Can an embedded consultant work in our time zone?**
Yes, within an agreed window. A remote consultant in India can typically overlap US Eastern mornings, most of the UK and European working day, Gulf business hours or Australian afternoons. The specific hours, meetings and response expectations should be written into the engagement.

**Can a consultant later become a permanent hire?**
Sometimes, if all parties agree and the arrangement allows it. It is better to decide up front whether the engagement is intended as a trial for a permanent role and to set the terms accordingly than to negotiate it under pressure later.

# Time Zone Overlap With an India Engineering Team | MV.tech Solutions

URL: https://mvtech.solutions/insights/timezone-overlap-with-an-india-based-engineering-team/
Description: Realistic overlap windows, what to agree up front and the async habits that make a remote team in India work for US, UK, EU and Australian companies.
Last modified: 2026-11-23

Remote delivery playbook

## How to Work with an India-Based Engineering Team Across Time Zones

Realistic overlap windows, what to agree up front and the async habits that make a remote team in India work for US, UK, EU and Australian companies.

By Meet Vaghasia, Founder & Lead Engineer · Published September 10, 2026 · Updated November 23, 2026 · 6 min read

In brief

- India Standard Time (UTC+5:30) overlaps the working day of every major business region for part of the day, so the question is never "is overlap possible?" but "which hours, and what happens outside them?"
- Agree four things before work starts: the collaboration window, where decisions get recorded, response expectations, and release windows. Most time zone problems are really unwritten-expectation problems.
- Treat "24/7 coverage" claims and unnamed engineers as warning signs. Ask for the specific hours and the specific people.
Companies hesitate about remote teams in India for one reason more than any other: the clock. The worry is reasonable, and it is also solvable, because it is mostly a planning problem rather than a geography problem. This guide covers what realistic overlap looks like from different regions, what to agree before an engagement begins, and the working habits that make distributed delivery feel closer than it is.

### Where India sits on the clock

India Standard Time is UTC+5:30 all year; India does not observe daylight saving. That places an Indian working day roughly like this relative to other regions:

- United Kingdom and Europe:India is 4.5 to 5.5 hours ahead of London and 3.5 to 4.5 hours ahead of Berlin, depending on the season. An engineer working a standard Indian day shares most of the UK and European morning and early afternoon.
- North America:India is 9.5 to 10.5 hours ahead of US Eastern time and 12.5 to 13.5 hours ahead of Pacific. A standard Indian day barely touches the US morning, so teams that serve American clients shift their hours later, typically starting around midday IST, to cover the US morning.
- Gulf:India is only 1.5 hours ahead of Dubai. Overlap is almost the whole day.
- Asia-Pacific:India is 2.5 hours behind Singapore and 4.5 to 5.5 hours behind Sydney, so Australian afternoons coincide with Indian mornings.
The practical conclusion: a team in India can give a European client a half-day of overlap without any adjustment, and can give an American client three to four hours every morning by shifting its day. It cannot give a single client both a full US afternoon and a full Australian morning with the same people, and any vendor who implies otherwise is describing something other than a normal working week.

### Typical overlap windows

These are the windows we plan engagements around at MV.tech Solutions. Yours may differ; the point is that they are specific.

Illustrative collaboration windows for a team in Ahmedabad, India
| Your team | Overlap in your local time | Equivalent in IST |
| New York (US Eastern) | 9:00 am – 1:00 pm | 6:30 pm – 10:30 pm during EDT7:30 pm – 11:30 pm during EST |
| San Francisco (US Pacific) | 7:00 am – 10:00 am | 7:30 pm – 10:30 pm during PDT8:30 pm – 11:30 pm during PST |
| London | 9:00 am – 3:30 pm | 1:30 pm – 8:00 pm during BST2:30 pm – 9:00 pm during GMT |
| Berlin (Central Europe) | 9:00 am – 4:00 pm | 12:30 pm – 7:30 pm during CEST1:30 pm – 8:30 pm during CET |
| Dubai (Gulf) | 9:00 am – 6:00 pm | 10:30 am – 7:30 pm |
| Singapore | 11:00 am – 6:00 pm | 8:30 am – 3:30 pm |
| Sydney (Australia East) | 12:30 pm – 6:00 pm | 7:00 am – 12:30 pm during AEDT8:00 am – 1:30 pm during AEST |
Write the window into the agreement in your local time. If you need a 9 am New York handover all year, your Ahmedabad team will move it an hour later in India when New York returns to standard time.

### Four things to agree before the first sprint

#### 1. The collaboration window, in your time

Write down the recurring hours during which the team is reachable synchronously, which meetings live inside them, and who attends. "Flexible" is not a window. "9:00 am to 1:00 pm Eastern, Monday to Friday, with standup at 9:15" is.

#### 2. Where decisions live

Distributed teams fail when decisions are made in a call and then forgotten by the half of the team that was asleep. Choose one place, such as a decision log in your wiki, pull request descriptions or a pinned channel, and make "write it down where the other side will see it" a habit, not a favor.

#### 3. Response expectations outside the window

Say explicitly what "urgent" means, how it is raised, and what response is expected outside the window. Most engagements need no out-of-hours coverage at all; production systems that do need it should have it written into the scope with named responsibilities, not implied by a sales conversation.

#### 4. Release windows

Decide when changes may reach production and who must be awake when they do. A team that deploys during the client's morning, with the client's own engineers online, avoids most of the drama associated with remote delivery.

### Async habits that actually work

- Written standups.Three lines per person, posted before the client's day begins: done, next, blocked. Ten minutes of reading replaces a meeting nobody wanted at 7:00 am.
- Recorded demos.A five-minute screen recording of a working feature, shared in the channel, lets stakeholders review at their convenience and reply with timestamps.
- Pull requests that explain themselves.What changed, why, how it was tested, what to look at first. Reviews then happen across the time gap instead of waiting for a call.
- Handover notes at the end of each day.Where things stand, what was decided, what needs an answer. The other side starts its morning informed rather than guessing.
- One synchronous ritual that never moves.A weekly review inside the window, with a demo and a look at the plan. Everything else can flex; this cannot.

### What should still be synchronous

Discovery conversations, design decisions with real trade-offs, incident response, and anything involving disagreement. If a thread has gone back and forth three times without converging, book fifteen minutes inside the window and settle it. Async is a default, not a religion.

### Warning signs when evaluating a remote vendor

- "We provide 24/7 support"from a team of five. Ask who exactly is awake at 3:00 am your time and what they are authorized to do.
- No named engineersbefore signing. If you cannot meet the people who will do the work, you are buying a promise, not a team.
- A dedicated account manageras the main contact. Useful in a large program, but for a small engagement it usually means the engineers are somewhere behind a wall.
- Vague overlap."We adjust to your time zone" without hours attached is a sentence, not a commitment.

### Which hours are included in the quote?

If an overnight pipeline fails half an hour before your London office opens, who checks it? Give each provider the same scenario. Ask for the engineer’s working hours, any separate on-call fee and who takes over when the shift ends. Our offshore data engineering team service sets out how we agree those responsibilities. If you’re budgeting for individual engineers, you can also compare the cost of an embedded engineer with a scoped project.

### Frequently asked questions

**Does India observe daylight saving time?**
No. India Standard Time stays at UTC+5:30 all year. Overlap windows written in a client's local time shift by an hour in IST when the client's region changes its clocks, which is why the window should be defined in the client's time.

**Can a team in India cover US Pacific hours?**
Yes. For example, 7 am to 10 am in San Francisco is 7:30 pm to 10:30 pm in Ahmedabad during Pacific daylight time and 8:30 pm to 11:30 pm during Pacific standard time. For afternoon or after-hours coverage, agree separately who will be on shift.

**How much overlap does a software project really need?**
In our experience, three to four hours of daily overlap is enough for standups, reviews, pairing on hard problems and releases, provided decisions and progress are written down. More overlap is pleasant; it is rarely what determines whether a project succeeds.

# Cost of a Remote Data Engineering Team from India | MV.tech Solutions

URL: https://mvtech.solutions/insights/what-a-remote-data-engineering-team-from-india-costs/
Description: What sets the price of a remote data engineering team from India, where the saving really comes from, how to compare quotes and the costs buyers forget.
Last modified: 2026-11-14

Cost guide

## What Does a Remote Data Engineering Team from India Cost?

What sets the price of a remote data engineering team from India, where the saving really comes from, how to compare quotes and the costs buyers forget.

By Meet Vaghasia, Founder & Lead Engineer · Published October 12, 2026 · Updated November 14, 2026 · 6 min read

In brief

- Five things set the price of a remote data engineering team: seniority, engagement shape, scope, overlap hours and support. Geography adjusts the number; it does not set it.
- The India cost difference comes mostly from what a lean remote consultancy is not paying for: offices in expensive cities, account-management layers, idle bench capacity and a brand premium. Senior engineers in India are not cheap.
- Compare quotes on the same scope, seniority and support, then add your own management, onboarding, access and documentation time before deciding which is cheaper.
Search for the cost of an offshore data team in India and the first answer is usually a single hourly number. It is rarely the price you pay, because it leaves out who does the work and what happens after the build.

### What determines the price of a remote data engineering team?

Five variables set the price: seniority, engagement shape, scope, overlap hours and support. A quote that gives a number without stating all five is a guess with a currency symbol in front of it.

- Seniority.A senior engineer who designs the model, writes the checks and reviews others' work costs more per hour than a mid-level engineer building to a specification, and usually less per finished outcome.
- Engagement shape.Hourly time, a retainer for a named person, a pod of a lead plus two or three engineers, or a fixed-scope project each price differently. See theengagement-model comparison.
- Scope.Source count, access complexity, historical volume, transformation rules, freshness requirements and how many dashboards depend on the result.
- Overlap hours.A standard Indian working day already covers most of the UK and European morning. Covering US mornings means shifting the team's day; a full US afternoon is unrealistic in a normal week. Thetime zone overlap guidegives realistic windows.
- Support.Build-and-hand-over is one price. Monitoring, maintenance, named out-of-hours response and agreed fix times are another, and should be written down.

### Why is a team in India cheaper, and where does the saving come from?

The difference comes from structure, not cheap labor. A lean remote consultancy is not paying for offices in expensive cities, account-management layers between you and the engineers, idle bench capacity or a brand premium, and it passes that structural difference through to the quote.

Pay does differ by country, and the benchmarks below show how much. But a consultancy's rate is not its engineers' salary: it also covers employer costs, tooling, non-billable review time, the gap between hours worked and hours sold, and margin. A quote that looks like a salary divided by working hours is leaving something out or describing a different level of engineer.

### What do public benchmarks say about data engineering rates?

Published figures put independent US consulting firms at $100 to $325 an hour depending on seniority, nearshore teams at $45 to $95, and senior data engineer pay in India at $19,000 to $37,000 a year against $180,000 or more in the US. Treat them as a sanity check, not a price list.

Public benchmark figures for data engineering rates and pay, all vendor-published and accessed October 12, 2026
| Benchmark | Published figure (USD) | Source and status |
| Independent US consulting firms, hourly by seniority | Mid-level $100–175; senior $150–250; principal $200–325 | bdemerson.com; vendor-published, accessed October 12, 2026 |
| Global consultancies, hourly | $250–450 | bdemerson.com; vendor-published, accessed October 12, 2026 |
| Nearshore teams, hourly | $45–95 | bdemerson.com; vendor-published, accessed October 12, 2026 |
| Pod of a lead plus two or three engineers, per month | $40,000–80,000 onshore; $25,000–50,000 blended nearshore | bdemerson.com; vendor-published, accessed October 12, 2026 |
| Fixed-scope projects | First warehouse builds from about $50,000; enterprise migrations $250,000 to over $1,000,000 | bdemerson.com; vendor-published, accessed October 12, 2026 |
| Freelance data engineer, hourly, all levels and regions | $73–184 | secondtalent.com; vendor-published, accessed October 12, 2026 |
| Freelance mid-level data engineer, hourly by region | US $92–145; Western Europe $49–77; Latin America $48–75; Southeast Asia $41–64 | secondtalent.com; vendor-published, accessed October 12, 2026 |
| India data engineer annual pay, 2026 | Junior $4,000–8,500; mid $8,500–19,000; senior $19,000–37,000 | wisemonk.io; vendor-published, accessed October 12, 2026 |
| US senior data engineer annual pay | $180,000 or more | wisemonk.io; vendor-published, accessed October 12, 2026 |
Sources: bdemerson.com, data engineering consulting rates; secondtalent.com, cost to hire a data engineer; wisemonk.io, cost of an offshore data foundation team in India. All three are vendor-published, and none of the figures above is an India consulting rate.

Three different things are measured here: consultancy billing rates, freelance rates and employee salaries, and they are not interchangeable. The India rows are pay, not what a consultancy charges, and the Southeast Asia band is a different region. Seniority moves the number as much as geography does.

### How do you compare offshore, nearshore and onshore quotes like for like?

Put every quote on the same basis: the same written scope, the same named seniority, the same overlap window and the same support terms, then convert each to a monthly cost at the capacity you will actually use. An hourly rate on its own compares nothing.

- Fix the scope in writingand send the same document to every vendor.
- Ask who, by name and level."A senior engineer" means little until you know whether that person designs the model or only builds to it.
- State the overlap window in your local timeand ask each vendor to price it. Nearshore may win on overlap and lose on seniority; India may be the reverse.
- List what is included:testing, reconciliation against today's numbers, documentation, handover, monitoring and post-launch fixes.
- Convert to a monthly figureat the hours you will use, including minimum commitments, ramp-up and notice terms.
The twelve questions to ask before hiring a remote data consultancy turn this into a checklist to send with the brief.

### Which costs do buyers forget?

The four costs that rarely appear in a quote are your own management time, onboarding, access and documentation. They exist in every delivery model and are larger when the team is remote, so they belong in the comparison.

- Management time.Someone on your side makes decisions, answers questions and reviews work.
- Onboarding.The first two to four weeks are slower: environment set-up, reading existing code, learning which numbers people trust.
- Access.Accounts, VPN, repositories, warehouse roles and SaaS tools take time from your IT and security teams.
- Documentation.If it is not in the quote, it will either not exist or be written by you. Runbooks, source-to-target mappings and recovery notes are what let you change vendors later.

### How does MV.tech Solutions price a remote data engineering team?

Pricing is agreed per engagement, and we quote after a scoping call. The model is lean and remote, which keeps office and management overhead low, so compare the quote on agreed scope, senior delivery time, validation, handover and support. The call covers the problem, the source systems, the target warehouse or BI tools, the timeline and the overlap window; a sanitized example is enough and credentials are not needed for an inquiry.

### Frequently asked questions

**Is an hourly rate or a monthly pod cheaper for data engineering work?**
It depends on how steady the work is. Hourly suits short or uncertain work and part-time specialists. A monthly pod or retainer usually costs less per hour for continuous work, but commits you to that capacity whether or not the backlog fills it. Convert both to a monthly figure at the hours you will really use.

**Is an offshore team in India cheaper than a nearshore team?**
Usually, at the same seniority, yes, but none of the figures above is an India consulting rate, so test it against your own quotes. The gap narrows once you add the overlap hours a US client may need. Nearshore teams often win on shared working hours; India-based teams often win on senior engineering cost.

**Why is there no rate card on this page?**
Because a rate without the seniority, scope, overlap and support attached would mislead more than it informs. We quote after a scoping call so the number reflects the actual work and the named people doing it.

### Scope a remote data team with MV.tech Solutions

Read what an offshore data engineering team from India can own, from pipelines and cloud warehouses to BI and migration support, then book a scoping call with the problem, the systems involved and the hours you need. We quote after that call.

# What Is Agentic AI? When to Build an AI Agent | MV.tech Solutions

URL: https://mvtech.solutions/insights/what-is-agentic-ai-and-when-does-a-business-need-an-ai-agent/
Description: Agentic AI in plain language: how an AI agent differs from a chatbot or an automation, when one is worth building, what keeps it safe and a first project.
Last modified: 2026-11-26

AI engineering

## What Is Agentic AI, and When Does a Business Need an AI Agent?

Agentic AI in plain language: how an AI agent differs from a chatbot or an automation, when one is worth building, what keeps it safe and a first project.

By Meet Vaghasia, Founder & Lead Engineer · Published November 26, 2026 · 6 min read

In brief

- Agentic AI means AI systems that work toward a goal over several steps: they decide what to do next, use tools such as a database query or a business API, check the result and continue until the task is done or a person needs to step in.
- An agent is worth building when a task runs through several systems, involves small judgment calls and has a clear finish. When the steps never change, a regular automation is cheaper and easier to test.
- What makes an agent safe is the engineering around the model: permission checks on the server, separate read and write tools, human approval for consequential actions, an evaluation set and a log of every step.
Most businesses met generative AI as a chat window: you ask, it answers. Agentic AI is the next step. Instead of producing a reply and stopping, an AI agent takes a request, works out the steps, uses your systems to carry them out and reports what it did. That makes it far more useful, and it also means the questions change from "is the answer good?" to "what is it allowed to do, and how do we know it did the right thing?"

### What agentic AI means

An AI agent is a language model placed in a loop with tools. The model reads the request and the current situation, chooses an action, such as looking up an order, running a query or drafting an email, and receives the result. It then decides the next action, and repeats until the goal is met or it reaches a point where it must hand over to a person.

The model provides the reasoning. Everything else is ordinary software: the tools it can call, the permissions on those tools, the checks on its inputs and outputs, and the record of what happened. In a well-built agent, most of the effort goes into that surrounding software, not into the prompt.

### Agent, assistant or automation?

Three kinds of system often get the same "AI" label. They suit different work.

How an AI agent compares with an assistant and a regular automation
| System | What it does | Best for |
| Regular automation | Follows fixed steps you define, every time | Repetitive work where the steps and inputs do not change |
| AI assistant | Answers questions or drafts text from your documents and data | Finding information and preparing first drafts that a person sends |
| AI agent | Plans steps and takes actions in your systems toward a goal | Multi-step tasks with judgment calls and a clear finish |
Many good projects combine them. An assistant that answers policy questions can later gain one agent ability, such as filing a request, once its answers are trusted. An agent can hand fixed sub-steps to a regular automation where that is more reliable.

### When an AI agent is worth building

- The task crosses several systems.A person opens the ticketing tool, the CRM and the order system to resolve one request. An agent can do the lookups and assemble the answer.
- It involves small judgment calls.Which category a request belongs to, which customer record matches, whether a document is complete. Fixed rules handle these badly; a model handles them well enough when the result is checked.
- It has a clear finish."Route this request with a drafted reply" is a good goal. "Improve customer service" is not.
- It happens often enough to matter.An agent pays off on work a team does every day or every week, not once a quarter.

### When it is not

- The steps never change.A regular automation is cheaper, faster and easier to test.
- A mistake would be costly and nobody can approve in time.If there is no sensible point for a person to check the action, the agent should draft, not act.
- The data it needs is not reachable or not clean.An agent cannot fix missing access or unreliable records; it will only move faster on bad information.

### What makes an AI agent safe enough for real work

The model will occasionally misread a request or choose the wrong tool. A production agent is designed so that those mistakes are caught or contained, rather than assuming they will not happen.

- Permissions on the server, not in the prompt.Each tool checks who the agent is acting for and what that person may access before it runs.
- Separate read and write tools.Looking things up and changing records are different tools with different rules. Most agents start read-only.
- Human approval for consequential actions.Sending, paying, deleting or changing anything important waits for a person, and the approval happens outside the model's control.
- Limits enforced in code.Caps on spending, request rates, record counts and run time stop a confused agent from doing damage at scale.
- An evaluation set.A collection of real requests with expected outcomes, run before every change to the prompt, tools or model.
- A log of every step.Which tool was called, with what input, and what came back. This is how a team reviews decisions and spots problems early.
If a tool returns content from an email, a web page or a document, the agent should treat it as data, not as instructions. This is the main defense against prompt injection, where text inside a document tries to redirect the agent.

### What a sensible first agent project looks like

- Pick one processyour team runs every week, with a clear finish and a clear owner.
- Collect real examples, typically fifty to a few hundred past requests with the outcome a person produced. These become the evaluation set.
- Start read-only: the agent looks things up and drafts, and a person acts. Measure how often the draft is right.
- Add one write action at a time, each behind an approval step, once the logs show the agent choosing tools reliably.
- Widen access gradually, from a small group of users to the whole team.
A focused first agent of this shape is usually weeks of work, and it leaves you with tools, tests and logs that the next agent can reuse.

### Frequently asked questions

**Is agentic AI the same as generative AI?**
Agentic AI is built on generative AI, but it is not the same thing. Generative AI produces text, images or code in response to a prompt. Agentic AI uses a generative model to decide on and carry out a series of actions with tools, working toward a goal rather than producing a single response.

**Do AI agents replace employees?**
In practice they take over parts of a job: the lookups, the copying between systems and the first draft. The person keeps the judgment calls, approves consequential actions and handles the exceptions the agent flags. Teams usually use the time saved on the work that needs a person.

**Can an AI agent work with the software we already use?**
Usually, yes, if the software has an API or a database the agent can reach through a controlled tool. Many teams expose those tools through an MCP server, so the same governed access works across several AI applications. Systems with no API can sometimes be reached through exports or a browser, but that is slower and more fragile.

**What does an AI agent cost to run?**
Running costs are mainly model usage, which grows with the number of requests and the number of steps each one takes, plus the hosting for the agent and its tools. Choosing a smaller model for simple steps, caching repeated lookups and capping the steps per request keep the cost predictable.

For the systems access underneath an agent, see MCP servers and AI connectors; for assistants that answer from your documents, see AI consulting. # What Is an MCP Server and When to Build One? | MV.tech Solutions

URL: https://mvtech.solutions/insights/what-is-an-mcp-server-and-when-should-a-business-build-one/
Description: The Model Context Protocol for business readers: what an MCP server exposes, when building one makes sense, the security decisions and a first project.
Last modified: 2026-11-26

AI engineering

## What Is an MCP Server, and When Should a Business Build One?

The Model Context Protocol for business readers: what an MCP server exposes, when building one makes sense, the security decisions and a first project.

By Meet Vaghasia, Founder & Lead Engineer · Published September 10, 2026 · Updated November 26, 2026 · 6 min read

In brief

- The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that lets AI applications connect to external tools and data through one consistent interface. An MCP server is the piece you build around your systems so that compatible AI assistants can use them.
- Build one when several AI clients need the same governed access to internal systems, when off-the-shelf connectors do not exist for your tools, or when you need authorization and logging in one place rather than in every prompt.
- Treat an MCP server as production software: authentication, least-privilege tool design, human approval for consequential actions and audit logs are part of the scope, not extras.
Every business that tries to make an AI assistant useful eventually hits the same wall: the assistant needs to look things up in, or act on, systems the model has never seen. Customer records, ticket queues, order status, internal documentation, the finance system. The Model Context Protocol is the emerging standard way to make those connections, and "MCP server development" has become a common request from teams who want their AI tools to do more than chat. This guide explains what an MCP server is in practical terms, when it is worth building one, and what to insist on if you do.

### What MCP is

MCP is an open protocol, originally released by Anthropic in late 2024 and since supported across the major AI assistant and developer platforms, that standardizes how an AI application (the client) discovers and uses capabilities offered by an external program (the server). The full specification and reference implementations are published at modelcontextprotocol.io.

Before MCP, connecting an assistant to a system meant writing a custom integration for each combination of assistant and system. With MCP, a system exposes its capabilities once, and any compatible client, whether a chat assistant, a coding tool or an internal agent, can use them the same way.

### What an MCP server exposes

- Tools:actions the assistant can call, with typed inputs and outputs. For examplelookup_order(order_id),create_ticket(summary, priority)orrun_approved_report(name, date_range).
- Resources:data the assistant can read, such as a document, a record or a query result, identified by a URI.
- Prompts:reusable, parameterized instructions that package a well-tested way of doing a task, for example "prepare a weekly status summary from these sources".
The server describes these capabilities in a machine-readable way, the client shows them to the model, and the model decides when to use them. The server, not the model, enforces what is allowed.

### When building an MCP server makes sense

- Your systems have no ready-made connector.Internal databases, custom applications, older business systems and in-house APIs rarely come with an MCP integration. Building one is how they join the conversation.
- Several AI clients need the same access.If your support assistant, your internal chat tool and a coding agent all need to read the same records, one server with consistent rules beats three bespoke integrations.
- Governance has to live in one place.An MCP server is where you enforce who may do what, log every call and shape which data leaves the system. That is far more reliable than instructions inside prompts.
- You want the assistant to act, not just answer.Creating tickets, updating records, triggering workflows: actions need typed inputs, validation and often human approval, which is exactly what a tool interface provides.

### When you probably do not need one

- One application, one model, one integration that will never be reused. A direct API call inside that application is simpler.
- The system you want to connect already has a well-maintained MCP server from its vendor. Evaluate it before building.
- The real problem is that the assistant cannot answer from documents. That is a retrieval problem; seeRAG versus fine-tuning. MCP can expose a retrieval tool, but the retrieval quality is the work.

### Security decisions you cannot skip

#### Authentication and identity

The server must know who is asking. Remote servers should use standards-based authentication, such as OAuth, and pass the user's identity through to the underlying systems so that existing permissions apply. A server that connects with one privileged service account on behalf of everyone is a data leak waiting for a clever prompt.

#### Least-privilege tool design

Expose narrow, purpose-built tools rather than "run any query" or "call any endpoint". Validate inputs, cap result sizes and separate read tools from write tools. The model will use whatever it is given; the server decides what that is.

#### Human approval for consequential actions

Anything that spends money, changes customer-facing records or sends communications should require an explicit confirmation step, either in the client's interface or in the workflow the tool triggers. Design the approval path into the tool, not around it.

#### Logging and audit

Record the caller, tool name, time, outcome and a request identifier. Keep arguments and results to an approved set of fields, mask secrets and personal data, and agree retention and access to the logs. An audit trail should help explain a call without creating another copy of confidential data. Review the protocol's security guidance alongside your own access requirements.

#### Untrusted content

Data returned by a tool may contain text that tries to instruct the model (a classic prompt injection). Servers should treat returned content as data, clients should display it as such, and consequential actions should never be triggered by content alone.

### What a sensible first MCP project looks like

- Pick one system and two or three toolsthat would remove real friction, for example looking up a customer, summarizing their recent tickets and drafting (not sending) a reply.
- Define the tool contractswith typed inputs, outputs, error cases and result limits, and agree which are read-only.
- Wire authenticationso the user's own permissions apply, and add logging from the first commit.
- Test with the intended clientsand with real tasks, including attempts to misuse the tools, before widening access.
- Document ownership and operation: who maintains the server, how it is deployed, how tools are added and reviewed.
A project of this shape is typically weeks of work, and it produces something you can extend tool by tool as trust grows.

### Frequently asked questions

**Is MCP tied to one AI vendor?**
No. MCP is an open specification with open-source SDKs in several languages, and it is supported by multiple AI assistants, developer tools and platforms. A server you build can be used by any compatible client, which is the main reason to prefer it over a bespoke integration.

**Does an MCP server need to be hosted on the internet?**
Not necessarily. Servers can run locally alongside a desktop client using standard input and output, or remotely over HTTP for shared use. Remote servers need proper authentication and network controls; local servers still need careful tool design because they run with the user's own access.

**What does MCP server development cost?**
The main cost drivers are the number and complexity of tools, the authentication model, the systems being integrated, testing and documentation. A focused first server with a handful of well-designed tools is a small project; the cost grows with the sensitivity of the actions it enables and the rigour those actions demand.

Before we begin

### Questions Hong Kong companies ask before outsourcing.

Not answered here? Ask us directly or read the full FAQ.

**When is your team available during Hong Kong hours?**
From about 11:00 am to 6:00 pm Hong Kong time, which is the Indian morning and early afternoon. Our team then works several more hours, so items raised late in your day usually have progress by the next morning.

**Do you deliver in English or Chinese?**
Meetings, documentation and code are in English. The applications and reports we build can carry Traditional Chinese content and interfaces, which your team reviews.

**How is personal data protected under the PDPO?**
The Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance keeps the data user responsible for how its processors handle personal data, including overseas. Most organizations keep personal data in their own environment with controlled access or masked data. We agree contractual terms with you before work starts.

**Can you work with our teams in Singapore or mainland China as well?**
Singapore and mainland China share Hong Kong’s time zone, so the same working window applies. Access to systems hosted in mainland China depends on your network and compliance rules, which we check at scoping.

**What size of project do you take on?**
From a single report or integration to a multi-month build with a dedicated team. We suggest starting with one milestone that can be accepted on its own.

### Questions New Zealand companies ask before outsourcing.

Not answered here? Ask us directly or read the full FAQ.

**Is the time difference between New Zealand and India workable?**
Yes, for work that can be written down and reviewed. We share about two and a half to three and a half hours late in your afternoon for calls and decisions. The rest runs on tickets, recorded walkthroughs and pull requests, and our team works while you are offline.

**What kind of work suits this arrangement, and what does not?**
Projects with clear requirements, backlog items, data pipelines and reporting suit it well. Work that needs constant real-time conversation, such as early product discovery or live incident response, needs more overlap than we can offer from India, and we will say so.

**How do you handle New Zealand privacy requirements?**
The Privacy Act 2020 restricts disclosing personal information overseas unless comparable safeguards are in place. Most organizations keep personal data in their own environment and give offshore engineers controlled access or masked data. We agree the terms with you before work starts.

**Can you also cover our Australian team?**
Yes. Sydney and Melbourne share a longer afternoon window with India, so a trans-Tasman team can use the Australian afternoon for joint sessions.

**How do we start?**
Send a short brief or book a call in the shared window. We reply with questions and a proposal that sets out scope, hours, people and price.

### Questions Singapore companies ask before outsourcing.

**What hours will we share with the team?**
Typically 11:00 am to 6:00 pm Singapore time, which is 8:30 am to 3:30 pm in India. Requests sent after that are picked up the same evening your time, because our team works for several more hours.

**How do you handle the PDPA when work is done from India?**
Giving engineers in India access to personal data is an overseas transfer under the PDPA, so the recipient must protect it to a comparable standard. **Can you support teams across Southeast Asia?**
Yes. Kuala Lumpur and Manila share Singapore’s time zone. Jakarta, Bangkok and Ho Chi Minh City are one hour behind, which lengthens the shared window by their clocks.

**Is offshoring to India suitable for a small Singapore company?**
Yes, if the first piece of work is small and specific. A first engagement can be one report, one integration or a part-time engineer, with a written milestone you accept before anything expands.

We quote after a scoping call. Projects are priced by milestone and dedicated engineers by agreed monthly capacity. The proposal states the currency and payment terms.

Not the full day, and we do not pretend otherwise. We typically share 9:00 am to 3:30 pm UK time, which covers stand-ups, reviews and most working sessions. Later requests are picked up the next morning in India, before your day starts.

**How do you handle UK GDPR when work is done from India?**
First we try to avoid moving personal data at all: engineers work in your environment, with test or masked data where the task allows. Where access to personal data from India is needed, your data protection lead will usually require an International Data Transfer Agreement or the UK Addendum, and those terms are settled before access is granted.

**Is this the same as hiring contractors?**
No. You contract with MV.tech Solutions as a company, for a scope of work or an agreed team capacity. The engineers are our team, we manage them, and continuity is our responsibility if someone is unavailable.

**What does it cost compared with a UK contractor or agency?**
We quote after a scoping call. Projects are priced by milestone and dedicated engineers by agreed monthly capacity. Compare proposals on the same deliverable, the seniority of the people and the support included, and count your own team’s time for reviews.

**Can you work with Dynamics 365 Business Central and Power BI?**
Yes. Finance reporting is a specialism: loading Business Central ledgers into a warehouse, reconciling supplier statements and month-end balances, and building Power BI reports that agree with the ledger.

Engineers use access you grant in your own cloud accounts, limited to what the work needs, and secrets stay in your secret manager. **What does outsourcing cost compared with hiring in the US?**
We quote after a scoping call, because the price depends on scope, seniority and the support you want us to own. A project is priced by milestone and a dedicated engineer by agreed monthly capacity. Compare that with the full cost of a US hire, including recruiting time, benefits and management.

**Can we start small?**
Yes. A first engagement can be one report, one integration or one part-time engineer. More scope is added after the first milestone is accepted.

# Privacy Policy | MV.tech Solutions

URL: https://mvtech.solutions/privacy/
Description: How MV.tech Solutions collects, uses and protects personal information on mvtech.solutions, and how US residents can exercise their privacy rights.
Last modified: 2026-11-23

Legal

## Privacy Policy

What personal information mvtech.solutions collects, why we collect it, who receives it and the choices you have. This policy covers this website and the inquiries you send us.

Last updated: November 23, 2026

### Who we are

MV.tech Solutions (“we”, “us”) operates mvtech.solutions. MV.tech Solutions is a registered assumed name (DBA) of BB & KV Inc., a New York corporation. Our headquarters is in Bellerose, New York, USA, and we have an office in Ahmedabad, India. Questions about this policy go to contact@mvtech.solutions.

### Information we collect

#### Information you give us

When you email us, send a project brief or book a call, we receive what you choose to share. That is usually your name, work email address, company, job title and phone number, and details about your project, systems, timeline and budget. Please do not send passwords, credentials or sensitive production data; we never need them for an inquiry.

If you use our short enquiry form, Google Forms stores your response in the MV.tech Solutions business account. We use the email address and project details you provide to reply to you. You can also contact us by email or book a call.

#### Information collected automatically

When analytics is active (see Cookies and analytics), Google Analytics records how the website is used: pages viewed, the page that referred you, approximate location (city or region, derived from your IP address), device and browser type, and clicks on our email, phone and booking links. Google Analytics 4 does not log or store IP addresses. Our hosting provider, GitHub Pages, processes the IP address of every visitor in order to deliver and protect the website.

#### Information from scheduling

If you book a call, Calendly collects the details you enter, such as your name, email address and any answers to booking questions, and shares them with us.

### Categories of personal information

Personal information we collect, where it comes from and who receives it
| Category | Examples | Source | Why we use it | Disclosed to |
| Identifiers | Name, email address, phone number | You | Reply to inquiries, schedule calls, prepare proposals | Our email and scheduling providers, and Google if you use the enquiry form |
| Professional information | Company, job title | You | Understand who we are working with | Our email and scheduling providers, and Google if you use the enquiry form |
| Commercial information | Project requirements, budget range | You | Scope and propose services | Our email provider, and Google if you use the enquiry form |
| Internet activity | Pages viewed, referring page, link clicks | Your browser, through Google Analytics | Improve the website | Google, as our analytics provider |
| Approximate location | City or region | Derived from your IP address | Understand where visitors come from | Google, as our analytics provider |
We do not collect sensitive personal information such as Social Security numbers, financial account details, precise geolocation or health information.

### How we use information

- To reply to your inquiry and keep in touch about it.
- To schedule and hold calls, prepare proposals and deliver services you agree to.
- To understand how the website is used and improve it.
- To protect the website and our business against fraud and abuse.
- To meet our legal, tax and accounting obligations.

### How we share information

We share personal information only with:

- Service providersthat run parts of our business for us: Google (website analytics and the optional enquiry form), Calendly (scheduling), our email provider and GitHub (website hosting). They may use it only to provide their services to us.
- Professional advisers, such as accountants and lawyers, who are bound by confidentiality.
- Authorities, when the law requires it or when needed to protect rights, property or safety.
- A successor business, if our business is reorganized or sold.
We do not sell personal information, and we do not share it for cross-context behavioral advertising or targeted advertising. Google Analytics runs on this website with Google signals and ad personalization turned off.

### Cookies and analytics

Google Analytics sets first-party cookies (named _ga and _ga_ followed by an ID) to tell visits apart. We do not use advertising cookies. Calendly sets its own cookies only when you load the booking calendar.

#### Global Privacy Control and Do Not Track

If your browser sends a Global Privacy Control (GPC) signal or a Do Not Track signal, this website does not load Google Analytics, and we treat the signal as a request to opt out of any sale or sharing of your personal information. You can also block cookies in your browser settings or install Google’s Analytics opt-out add-on.

#### Tracking by other companies

Apart from Google Analytics, and Calendly when you load the booking calendar, we do not allow other companies to collect personal information about your activity on this website over time or across other websites.

### Your privacy rights

Depending on the state you live in, US privacy laws, including those of California, Virginia, Colorado, Connecticut, Texas and Oregon, give you the right to:

- know what personal information we hold about you, and receive a copy of it;
- correct inaccurate personal information;
- delete your personal information;
- opt out of the sale or sharing of personal information, targeted advertising and profiling (we do none of these); and
- use these rights without being treated differently.
We honor these requests from any US resident, whether or not a state law requires it.

#### How to make a request

Email contact@mvtech.solutions with “Privacy request” in the subject line and tell us what you would like us to do. We confirm receipt within 10 business days and respond within 45 days. We may ask you to confirm details that show the request is yours, such as the email address you used to contact us. An authorized agent may make a request for you with your signed permission.

#### Appeals

If we decline a request, you can appeal by replying with “Privacy appeal” in the subject line. We respond to appeals within 45 days. If you remain unsatisfied, you may contact the attorney general of your state.

### How long we keep information

- Inquiry emails, form responses and booking details:as long as needed to respond to you and, for clients, for the length of the relationship plus the period our legal, tax and accounting records require.
- Analytics data:for the retention period set in Google Analytics, never longer than 14 months.

### Security

We protect personal information with reasonable safeguards for its sensitivity, including limiting access to the people who need it. No method of sending or storing information is completely secure.

### Where information is processed

Our team works in the United States and India. Personal information you send us may be accessed by our team in India and processed by our service providers in the United States and other countries.

### Children

This website is for businesses and is not directed to children under 13. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13, and we do not sell the personal information of anyone under 16. If you believe a child has sent us personal information, contact us and we will delete it.

### Data we handle for clients

Data we work with while delivering services for a client is governed by that client’s agreement with us, not by this policy. Our approach is described in our security and delivery standards.

### Links to other websites

This website links to websites we do not control, such as LinkedIn and Calendly. Their own privacy policies apply when you visit them.

### Changes to this policy

We post any change on this page and update the date at the top. If a change materially affects how we use personal information you have already given us, we will tell you by email before it takes effect.

### Contact us

Email contact@mvtech.solutions, or write to either of our offices.

# Software, Data & AI Project Delivery Process | MV.tech Solutions

URL: https://mvtech.solutions/process/
Description: How MV.tech Solutions plans and delivers engineering work: discovery, architecture, development, testing, deployment, documentation and agreed ongoing support.
Last modified: 2026-11-14

Delivery process

## From business requirements to production delivery.

MV.tech Solutions delivers software, data and AI work through a planned engineering process. The scope covers the stages your project requires, from discovery and architecture through development, testing, deployment and handover.

Delivery lifecycle

### What happens at each stage.

#### Discovery and requirements

Work with business and technical stakeholders to understand users, workflows, source systems and constraints. Review existing code, data and integrations where relevant, and document open questions and dependencies.

#### Architecture and delivery planning

Agree the technical approach, release priorities, responsibilities and acceptance criteria. Set out the integrations, access, environments and client inputs needed for delivery.

#### Development and integration

Build in reviewable stages. Demonstrate working features, pipelines or reports, record decisions and incorporate agreed feedback into the delivery plan.

#### Testing and acceptance

Test the agreed business workflows and integrations. Reconcile important data, review permissions and check failure handling and performance requirements relevant to the system.

#### Deployment and transition

Plan the release, environment configuration and any migration or rollback steps. Confirm operating ownership, monitoring and the acceptance process before moving into use.

#### Handover and ongoing support

Provide the agreed code, configuration and operating documentation. Review maintenance, enhancements, training or continuing engineering capacity as separate ongoing requirements.

Client collaboration

### Keep decisions close to the people who own them.

We agree the project’s working rhythm and decision responsibilities at the start.

- Business and product input. Your stakeholders clarify priorities, review workflows and confirm that the output meets the business requirement.
- Technical ownership. Agree who reviews architecture, code, data definitions, access and releases across both teams.
- Working hours and reviews. Schedule recurring collaboration in the agreed time zone window and document progress and decisions between meetings.
- Scope changes. Review the effect of new requirements on delivery, cost and dependencies before adding them to the engagement.
Project outputs

### What the agreed delivery can include.

#### Planning and design

Requirements, source mappings, architecture decisions, delivery milestones and acceptance criteria.

#### Working implementation

Application code, data pipelines, models, reports or integrations, with the tests and configuration needed to run them.

#### Operating documentation

Deployment instructions, schedules, access definitions, monitoring and handover notes for the system in scope.

Questions about working with us

### What you need to know.

**Can you join an existing project?**
Yes. We can review the relevant code, platform or reporting setup and take on a defined workstream. The onboarding scope depends on the documentation, access and current state of the system.

**How often will we review progress?**
We agree the review schedule with your team before delivery. Reviews use working software, data outputs or reports, supported by written decisions and progress updates.

**Do you provide maintenance after launch?**
Maintenance, support and further development can be agreed after or alongside the project. Coverage, response expectations and responsibilities are defined separately from meeting overlap.

**Who owns the deliverables?**
Ownership, repository access, licensing and handover responsibilities are set out in the engagement terms. Raise any procurement or intellectual-property requirements during scoping.

Contact MV.tech Solutions

### Plan the delivery of your next project.

Tell us what you want to build, improve or connect. We’ll discuss the requirements, the delivery options and the people the work needs.

Before we begin

### Questions about hiring a remote data team in India

Not answered here? Ask us directly or read the full FAQ.

**Can a team in India overlap US, UK, European or Australian hours?**
Yes. India Standard Time (UTC+5:30) overlaps every major business region for part of the day. We typically plan 9:00 am to 1:00 pm US Eastern, 7:00 to 10:00 am US Pacific, 9:00 am to 3:30 pm in the UK, 9:00 am to 4:00 pm in Central Europe, most of the business day in the Gulf, and 12:30 to 6:00 pm in eastern Australia. Share your city and required hours and we agree the exact window for the engagement.

**Does time zone overlap mean 24/7 support?**
No. Overlap means agreed working hours for collaboration. Any support coverage, response expectations or release windows need to be defined in the engagement scope.

**Why can a remote consulting team have lower overhead?**
A focused remote model can avoid large office and account-management costs and keep clients closer to the specialists doing the work. The total project cost depends on scope, complexity and support; we agree the deliverables and commercial terms for each engagement.

**How can we assess the team's experience?**
Start with the work examples on our expertise page. Then ask the engineer who would join your project to walk through a similar technical decision, how they checked the result and what they would do differently in your setup.

**How much does a remote data team in India cost?**
Pricing is agreed per engagement and we quote after a scoping call. The total depends on scope, complexity and the support you need us to own, and a focused remote team keeps office and management overhead low. Compare proposals on agreed scope, senior delivery time, validation, handover and support so the figure reflects the work you actually need.

**What is the difference between staff augmentation and project consulting?**
With a scoped project, MV.tech Solutions owns the agreed delivery scope and we agree the milestone, acceptance criteria and handover first. With an embedded specialist, which is the staff augmentation model, your leads direct the consultant workstream and we agree skills, capacity, duration and overlap. If you need a permanent role in your organization, recruitment is a separate model where you select and employ the candidate.

MV.tech Solutions services

## Agentic AI and AI agents that complete work in your systems.

An AI agent does more than answer a question. It reads a request, decides which steps to take, uses your tools to carry them out and reports back. MV.tech Solutions designs and builds agents for real business tasks, with clear limits on what they can reach, approval steps for anything that changes a record, and logs your team can review.

- New York headquarters and Ahmedabad office

- Senior specialists, direct access

The starting point

### Use an agent when the work has several steps and a clear finish.

- A task takes a person through several systems and many small decisions, such as triaging requests, preparing a report or updating records.
- Your team already uses an AI assistant and wants it to complete work, not only draft text.
- A proof of concept works in a demo and needs permissions, testing and monitoring before real users depend on it.
What we deliver

01

Agents built around one business process, such as request triage, data lookups, document handling or report preparation. Each has a defined goal, a list of tools it may use and a clear point where it stops and hands over to a person.

The functions an agent calls to read or update your systems, built as APIs or MCP servers. Read and write tools are kept separate, inputs are validated, and every call runs under a scoped identity.

#### Approval steps and guardrails

Human approval before an agent sends, pays, deletes or changes anything that matters. Limits on scope, spending and request rates are enforced in code rather than in the prompt.

04

#### Evaluation and monitoring

A test set of real requests with expected outcomes, run before every change. A log of each step the agent took, so your team can review its decisions and spot problems early.

Before we begin

### Common questions about agentic AI and AI agents

Not answered here? Ask us directly or read the full FAQ.

**What is agentic AI?**
Agentic AI describes AI systems that work toward a goal over several steps. Instead of answering a single prompt, an agent decides what to do next, calls tools such as a database query or a business API, checks the result and continues until the task is done or it needs a person. The model does the reasoning; the tools, permissions and checks around it decide what it can actually do.

**How is an AI agent different from a chatbot?**
A chatbot answers questions. An agent takes actions. A chatbot over your HR policies tells an employee how to request leave; an agent could check the balance, fill in the request and send it to a manager for approval. Many projects start as an assistant that answers and add agent abilities once the answers are trusted.

**When is an AI agent the wrong choice?**
When the steps never change, a regular automation is cheaper, faster and easier to test. When a mistake would be costly and there is no sensible point for a person to approve, an agent should not act on its own. We will tell you if a simpler workflow, or an assistant that only drafts, is the better fit.

**How do you stop an AI agent from doing something it should not?**
By limiting what it can reach rather than relying on instructions. Each tool checks permissions on the server, write actions are separate from reads, consequential steps wait for human approval, and spending and request limits are enforced in code. Every step is logged, so unexpected behavior shows up in review.

**Which AI models do you build agents with?**
We work with Claude, GPT, Gemini and open models such as Llama and Qwen, and choose per task based on quality, cost, speed and where your data is allowed to go. The tools and the evaluation set are kept separate from the model, so you can change models later without rebuilding the agent.

**How much does it cost to build an AI agent?**
We quote after a scoping call. The main factors are the number of systems the agent uses, how many of its actions change data, your approval and audit requirements and the size of the evaluation set. A first agent for one process and one team is the usual starting point. Model usage is billed separately by the provider and depends on volume.

**How long does a first AI agent take to build?**
A focused first agent for one process usually takes weeks, not months. The first part maps the task and collects real test cases; the rest is build and evaluation rounds until the agent meets the agreed standard. A wider rollout follows once the logs show it behaving as expected.

Before we begin

### Questions buyers ask about RAG, LLM integration and AI agents

Not answered here? Ask us directly or read the full FAQ.

**What is retrieval-augmented generation, or RAG?**
RAG retrieves relevant material from an approved source collection and provides it to a language model when generating an answer. It can help an assistant answer questions about your own information, but retrieval quality, access controls and evaluation still matter.

**What is MCP development?**
Model Context Protocol (MCP) provides a shared interface for AI applications to connect to tools and data. We build MCP servers in Python around your approved APIs or systems, define the tools and resources they expose, handle authorization with OAuth and managed secrets, and test them with the intended compatible clients. Access permissions and approval requirements remain part of the application design.

**Can an AI agent query our databases safely?**
It can, when access is engineered rather than prompted. In practice that means a connector or MCP server that authenticates as a scoped service identity, exposes only approved tables or endpoints, generates SQL against a governed reporting layer, validates the query and the result before returning it, and logs every call. Whitelists and read-only access keep an agent away from anything it has no business touching.

**Do we need to train our own AI model?**
Not necessarily. The right scope may use an existing model with retrieval and application integration. We review your use case, data, evaluation criteria and operating constraints before proposing an approach.

**Can the assistant respect different user permissions?**
Role-aware access can be part of the scope. The design must enforce authorization before protected data is retrieved or an action is performed; instructions written into a prompt are not a substitute for application access controls.

**What determines the cost of an AI assistant?**
The main factors are source preparation, integrations, permission rules, evaluation, user interface and support. Ongoing costs also depend on model usage, retrieval infrastructure and traffic. These should be considered alongside the build estimate.

Before we begin

### Questions people ask before hiring a BigQuery consultant.

Not answered here? Ask us directly or read the full FAQ.

**How much does BigQuery consulting cost?**
We quote after a scoping call. The estimate depends on the number of sources, the volume of history to load, how much SQL needs translating, the reports in scope and whether you want support after handover. A first project is scoped to be verifiable in weeks, and the quote for anything beyond it is based on your own query history.

**Why is our BigQuery bill so high?**
Usually because queries read more than they need to. The common causes are tables with no partitioning, dashboards that query raw tables, scheduled queries that rebuild full history every hour and SELECT * in views that other views build on. The fix starts with the job history, which shows exactly which queries bill the most bytes and who runs them, and then applies partition filters, clustering, materialised views and per-user limits in that order.

**Should we partition BigQuery tables by ingestion time or by an event date column?**
By the column your queries filter on, which is usually an event or transaction date. Ingestion-time partitioning is simpler to load but only helps when reports ask about when data arrived, which they rarely do. Where late-arriving records are common, the load uses MERGE into the correct date partition rather than appending to today's, and a partition-filter requirement stops anyone scanning the full table by accident.

**Can you migrate us to BigQuery from SQL Server, PostgreSQL, Redshift or Snowflake?**
Yes. The work starts with discovery of what exists and what depends on it, then a source-to-target mapping per object, SQL translated and tested, and reconciliation of counts, totals and reported metrics at each layer before the old platform is switched off. Platform-specific SQL, stored procedures and cross-database joins are the usual blockers, and they are found in discovery rather than at cutover.

**Can a remote team in India run our BigQuery project?**
Yes. Our team works from New York and Ahmedabad, India, and agrees a collaboration window in your time zone before the engagement starts, which typically covers UK and European business hours, US Eastern mornings, Gulf hours or Asia-Pacific afternoons. Access is through your own Google Cloud project with IAM roles you grant and can revoke, logs stay in your project and no credentials are needed for an initial inquiry.

**Is Looker Studio good enough, or do we need Power BI?**
Looker Studio is reasonable for reporting over BigQuery when the model lives in the warehouse and the reports read curated views. Power BI becomes the better choice when you need a governed semantic layer, row-level security or complex measures, or when the organization already runs on Microsoft 365. Either way the metric definitions belong in BigQuery, so changing the reporting tool later is a repointing exercise rather than a rebuild.

**Is MV.tech Solutions a Google Cloud partner?**
No. MV.tech Solutions is not a Google partner. Its founder holds the Google Cloud Professional Data Engineer credential, which is an individual certification, and has built BigQuery pipelines in previous roles. If partner status matters for your procurement, say so on the first call.

- Reconciling ledger and dashboard totals
- Building read-only data connectors
Explore our expertiseTime zones, team and engagement costsOutsourcing by region
Before we begin

### Questions buyers ask about blockchain data analytics

Not answered here? Ask us directly or read the full FAQ.

**Why not just use a public chain dataset?**
Public datasets are a reasonable starting point for common chains and standard token transfers. They tend to fall short on newer or smaller networks, on contracts whose events are not standard, and on the business layer: your token registry, your categorization rules, your reporting currency and your reconciliation against internal records. We use public datasets where they fit and build ingestion where they do not.

**How do you handle a contract with no published ABI?**
Several ways, in order of preference: a verified ABI from the explorer, a standard interface the contract conforms to, an ABI supplied by whoever deployed it, or reconstruction from method signatures and observed event topics. Whichever route is used, the decoding rules are recorded per contract and the raw input data is retained, so decoding can be corrected and replayed without re-ingesting the chain.

**Can analysts correct a figure without breaking the audit trail?**
That is what the override layer is for. Base tables hold what the chain reported and are never edited. Corrections, whitelists and manual classifications live in separate tables with an author, a timestamp and a reason, and are applied when the reporting view is built. Both the original and the adjusted figure stay available, which is usually what an auditor asks to see.

**How do you value tokens that barely trade?**
Carefully, and visibly. The valuation method is a documented rule per token: reference price at block timestamp, a defined source hierarchy, a fallback, or explicitly no valuation at all. Unvalued volume is reported rather than hidden. It is better for a finance team to see that a share of activity has no reliable price than to receive a confident number built on a thin market.

**Can this feed our existing warehouse and dashboards?**
Yes. On-chain data is just another source: it lands in the same layered warehouse, under the same validation and modeling standards, and is read by Power BI, Looker Studio, Tableau or a Streamlit tool alongside everything else. Teams usually want it joined to off-chain records — customers, internal accounts, fiat movements — and that join is where most of the analytical value appears.

**How much does blockchain data analytics consulting cost?**
We quote after a scoping call, once the networks, contracts and wallets in scope, the reporting currency and period, and the figures the output has to reconcile against are agreed. A useful first project is a single chain and one business question built the whole way through, from ingestion and decoding to a reconciled output. Our team works from New York and Ahmedabad, India, with working hours planned around your time zone and a lean model that avoids large-consultancy overhead.

**How do you reconcile staking rewards against on-chain and internal records?**
We build a reward ledger per validator, delegator or wallet and reconcile it against on-chain distributions and internal records, with period totals, accrual timing and a discrepancy report. Base tables hold exactly what the chain reported and are never edited; corrections live in a separate override layer with an author, a timestamp and a reason, so both the original and adjusted figures stay available.

#### Business Intelligence & Dashboards

Give business teams a consistent view of performance.
